title: Disaster Preparedness

source.boundary: Actual Disaster Preparedness title on PDF1/printed19 through references above actual Natural Disasters title in right column PDF7/printed25. Running header on final page already says Chapter6; Chapter5 text above actual title remains eligible.
source.verification: Selected vocabulary and boundary verification, not current disaster practice or clinical recommendations.

scope: Eighteen selected terms. Candidate associations only, not exhaustive chapter coverage or original clinical narration. New chapter composition is not a claim of novel invention.

source_wording_notes.external disaster: Source includes plural external disasters; canonical headword singularized.
source_wording_notes.crossmatching: Source line-end cross-/matching normalized for matching.
source_wording_notes.tabletop triage scenarios: Exact source phrase; replaces preliminary working phrase tabletop exercises.

entries.cue: Detective using a magnifier to examine a cracked protective shield.
entries.cue_scope: Looking for hazards and weak protection
entries.reason: Inspection plus vulnerability provides a learned planning cue. Not a complete risk model, scoring method or checklist.

entries.cue: Damaging storm visibly inside a transparent hospital model.
entries.reason: Inside/outside carries the contrast without elaborate phonetics. Storm is a metaphor, not a claim that every internal disaster is weather-related.

entries.cue: Damaging storm outside a clearly bounded hospital model.
entries.reason: Complementary location cue uses the same hospital boundary as the internal cue. Does not imply that the hospital stays unaffected or cannot experience both event types.

entries.cue: Theatrical makeup kit beside a mannequin with clearly simulated wound makeup.
entries.reason: Direct visual identity is more useful than forcing an incomplete mule sound pun. Makeup kit and mannequin support the simulated context; no wound diagnosis or technique.

entries.cue: Miniature patient tokens and the familiar sorting tree arranged on a tabletop.
entries.prior: New chapter composition using the Chapter4 tree/triage primitive.
entries.reason: Tabletop context and miniatures express rehearsal. Reuses sorting grammar; no actual triage categories or patient-priority rules encoded.

entries.cue: Oversized hand pushing a packed medical supply crate.
entries.reason: Action plus packed supplies recovers the phrase. Does not encode shipment contents, delivery times, availability or agency policy.

entries.cue: Shower removing conspicuous surface stains from a protective-suit mannequin.
entries.reason: Familiar cleaning/removal association, not a universally applicable decontamination procedure. No chemical-specific method, fluid, duration or protection recommendation.

entries.cue: Additional open care spaces facing a wave of arrivals.
entries.reason: Established Chapter1 cue reused. Extra capacity must remain visible; crowd alone is demand, not capacity. No numerical capacity or staffing claim.

entries.cue: Person in a familiar hazmat-style protective suit.
entries.reason: Established category cue; no need to invent a different symbol. Not required equipment, protection rating or an agent-specific safety standard.

entries.cue: Tree with branching chutes sorting patient tokens.
entries.reason: Existing Chapter4 candidate reused consistently. No new triage algorithm or clinical classification encoded.

entries.cue: Clamp closes a pipe leaking red liquid.
entries.reason: Reuses user-inspired Chapter1 design. No patient clamping, tourniquet method or treatment selection.
User's established overflow example, not a new discovery. Not dietary causation, a serum value, a threshold or treatment instruction.

entries.cue: Limb mannequin compressed in a large vise.
entries.reason: Visible compression supplies an economical familiar injury cue. Not a time threshold, pathophysiology, diagnosis or treatment plan.

entries.cue: Kidney-shaped factory with conspicuously broken gears.
entries.reason: Functional breakdown links the renal identity and failure concept without forcing a sound bridge. Not a literal renal mechanism, laboratory criterion or automatic link to a specific cause.

entries.cue: Bank vault holding recognizable blood bags.
entries.reason: Familiar financial bank becomes a memorable storage identity. Not a blood-storage specification, stock requirement or handling guide.

entries.cue_scope: Cross plus matches name cue in blood context
entries.reason: Name bridge, not an explanation or result of compatibility testing. Does not imply blood is heated, burned or compatible because props match.
No convincing association proposed in this bounded pass. Do not fill the slot with generic gas imagery or forced sound fragments.

entries.cue: Rice visibly IN a clear container.
entries.reason: Rice plus in can provide a compact learned phrase bridge; pronunciation and naming remain untested. The clear boundary must show the in relationship. Never imply rice contains or produces ricin, or encode toxicology or preparation instructions.
